question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Decay-per-division vs. decay-per-hour: decoupling time from mitosis
ideas.description: Deliver a defined pulse of AP-1 activity (optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization or a degron-stabilized bZIP), then measure the decay of primed enhancer accessibility and of the amplified secondary response while independently varying proliferation rate (contact inhibition, serum, CDK4/6 inhibitors, or cell-cycle-arrested cells). Memory that dilutes as a function of cell divisions implicates a chromatin-templated carrier, whereas decay that tracks wall-clock time regardless of division implicates protein/RNA half-life, and the two models are quantitatively distinguishable from the decay curves alone.

ideas.title: Sister-cell splitting plus clonal barcoding to measure the heritability of AP-1 state
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with lineage barcoding, then physically split sister cells (or clonal subpopulations) and challenge one half while profiling the other, quantifying how much of a cell's future stimulus response is predicted by its own mother's prior AP-1 state versus population average. This converts 'memory' into an explicit heritability statistic (mother-daughter and sister-sister correlation as a function of generations elapsed), which can be compared head-to-head against DNA methylation or H3K27me3 as alternative carriers.

ideas.title: Tether-and-release: sufficiency of AP-1 at a single enhancer
ideas.description: Recruit the FOS/JUN bZIP or transactivation domain to one chosen naive enhancer with dCas9, then wash out or degrade the tether and ask whether that single element remains accessible, nucleosome-depleted, and hyper-responsive to later stimulation relative to unmanipulated alleles in the same nucleus. Allele-specific readouts (targeting one haplotype) give an internally controlled test of whether transient AP-1 occupancy is sufficient to install a persistent local state.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and daughter-cell inheritance of AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Use live single-molecule imaging of FOS/JUN residence times through mitosis plus mitotic CUT&RUN/ATAC and daughter-cell-resolved accessibility profiling to determine whether AP-1 retains, rapidly re-occupies, or entirely loses its binding sites across division. The decisive measurement is the timing of re-establishment in early G1 relative to global chromatin reopening: true bookmarking predicts AP-1 sites reopen first and in a parent-matched, allele-correlated pattern.

ideas.title: Acute post-encoding degradation: is AP-1 the memory or merely its reader?
ideas.description: Separate the encoding window from the maintenance window with an auxin/dTAG degron that removes AP-1 subunits only after a primed state has been established, then test whether the potentiated response survives the AP-1-free interval and returns when AP-1 is restored. Persistence without AP-1 would show that the factor writes and later interprets a memory stored elsewhere (nucleosome positioning, histone marks, or a cofactor), reframing AP-1 as a reader rather than the storage medium itself.
